clue.text: Excessive work previously in the public eye raised temperature

indicators.note: previously says that what follows in the clue comes before the word for work in the answer

parts.note: something in the public eye is overt, openly seen
het, as in 'het up', means heated, with a raised temperature
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone excessively busy in the past, now in the spotlight, is running a fever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'previously' puts OP (work) after the other two pieces, which the clue gives first.
explanation.definitionFit: Going beyond reasonable bounds is the idiomatic meaning of this phrase, a synonym for excessive.

clue.text: Single element in a set, reactive

definitions.text: Single element in a set, reactive

parts.note: A means one, single

indicators.note: something reactive changes on contact, so these letters react and rearrange

parts.note: tin is a chemical element
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chemistry note about one element among a group that reacts readily.
explanation.walkthrough: A and TIN go in with A SET, and 'reactive' turns the eight letters into the halogen. The whole clue also describes it: one radioactive element of the halogen set.
explanation.definitionFit: Astatine is a single radioactive halogen, one element of that chemical group.

clue.text: See 16
Carry on with payment

definitions.meaning: to carry on a campaign or war is to ... it
a regular payment for work, such as weekly pay

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to conduct a war or campaign, and earnings paid for labour.

clue.text: Socialist experienced endlessly rising pain on his wrong side?

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the piece is read upwards, backwards
endlessly means the word for experienced loses its final letter

parts.note: to have experienced pain is to have felt it
a twinge is a sudden sharp pain
for a person of the left, the wrong side is the right, abbreviated R

explanation.surface: A socialist suffers a pain that keeps getting worse, on the side he dislikes.
explanation.walkthrough: FELT loses its end ('endlessly') to give FEL, and 'rising' turns it up to LEF. The question mark flags the joke that a leftie's wrong side is the right.
explanation.definitionFit: A left-winger is a person on the political left, such as a socialist.

clue.text: Gwynedd resort will help with repairs

indicators.note: repairs suggest the letters are taken apart and put back together differently

explanation.surface: A Welsh seaside town promises that fixing things up will help.
explanation.walkthrough: Gwynedd is a county in north-west Wales; Pwllheli is a seaside town on the Llyn peninsula there.
explanation.definitionFit: Pwllheli is a seaside holiday town in Gwynedd, north Wales.

clue.text: Do one in possession of gold crown

indicators.note: being in possession of something means holding it, so the first pieces hold the second

parts.note: to do someone is to con or swindle them
OR is the heraldic word for gold
A means one

explanation.surface: Someone cheating, having got hold of a gold crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a verb of action but means swindle; 'in possession of' makes the first pair hold the heraldic gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Corona is Latin for crown, used for a crown-shaped part or the sun's halo.

clue.text: See 16
Complete dependency when rescue's very far westward?

indicators.note: in an across answer west is the left, so the letter goes all the way to the front

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
salvage is rescue of goods; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Total reliance on others when help arrives from a long way west.
explanation.walkthrough: AS + SALVAGE makes ASSALVAGE; moving the V far west, to the very front, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Vassalage was the feudal condition of a vassal, total subjection to a lord.

clue.text: In verse, the frog's women could be interpreted in a naughty way!

parts.words: could be interpreted in a naughty way
parts.note: 'ooer' is the comic British exclamation that points out an unintended double meaning

explanation.surface: A nursery rhyme frog has women who might read things smuttily.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'A frog he would a-wooing go' makes the frog a suitor. 'Ooer' is a British comedy exclamation at an accidental innuendo, as in Frankie Howerd.
explanation.definitionFit: In the rhyme the frog goes courting, so he is a suitor seeking a bride.

clue.text: Accomplish 4 increase without the brewing of ale

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: 4-down is WAGE, and a wage increase is a rise

indicators.note: brewing works ingredients into something new, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Raising pay while leaving out the beer that's being brewed.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' points to the answer of 4-down; a wage increase in British English is a rise. 'without' means outside, and 'the brewing of' rearranges the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise a plan or ambition is to achieve or accomplish it.

clue.text: Fish sign mentioned in exam

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a test is an exam
Leo is a sign of the zodiac named here

explanation.surface: A star sign comes up in an exam about fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Teleosts are the bony fish, the largest group of fishes.

clue.text: In a hurry, as Billy Connolly in Wells

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: H. G. Wells, the novelist, gives his initials
the Scottish comedian Billy Connolly is called the Big Yin, yin being Scots for one

explanation.surface: Billy Connolly rushing about in the Somerset city of Wells.
explanation.walkthrough: Wells looks like the cathedral city but is the author H. G. Wells. Billy Connolly, Scottish comedian, is nicknamed 'the Big Yin'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hying is the present participle of hie, an archaic verb meaning to hasten.

clue.text: See 16
Pentecost's the reason for holding its United Nations poster up

indicators.note: holding means the first piece contains the rest

parts.note: why asks for the reason
taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: an ad is a poster or advertisement

explanation.surface: A church feast explained by its United Nations poster being put up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the poster in this down clue, and 'holding' puts the inner pieces inside the question word.
explanation.definitionFit: Whit Sunday is the British name for Pentecost, the seventh Sunday after Easter.

clue.text: Sinister affair that carries much weight universally?

parts.note: something sinister is dark
an affair is a matter or business

explanation.surface: A shady business that has great influence everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries much weight' looks figurative, but cosmologists think this invisible substance makes up most of the universe's mass.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark matter is the unseen material thought to make up most of the mass in the universe.

clue.text: A certain emotional pointer's an author and, once summonsed, puts setback behind him (OK, in short)

parts.note: a pointer is a finger, and emotional means stirring or touching; the 's is 'is'
to be an author is to compose text
taken as written
a person summonsed has been served a court document in the past
to put a setback behind you is to go forward and leave it

explanation.surface: A touching gesture belongs to an author who, once sued, gets past his trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: OK stands for Omar Khayyam: the line is from FitzGerald's translation of the Rubaiyat. Each piece of the clue is a cryptic gloss on a stretch of the quotation.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous couplet from Omar Khayyam's Rubaiyat in FitzGerald's English version, with OK abbreviating the poet.

clue.text: Preoccupied bosses unsettled leader-writer

indicators.note: unsettled means disturbed, so the letters are moved about

parts.note: a newspaper's leaders are written by its editor, ED

explanation.surface: Bosses rattled by the newspaper columnist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettled' rearranges BOSSES to OBSESS; a leader is a newspaper editorial, so its writer is ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone obsessed is preoccupied, thinking constantly about one thing.

clue.text: Suspicious behaviour? Enter and get fantastic snog!

parts.note: to enter is to go in

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something fanciful, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An invitation to come inside for a terrific kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: Snog is British slang for a passionate kiss; 'fantastic' rearranges it after the phrase for entering.
explanation.definitionFit: Goings-on are dubious or underhand activities, often hinted at with suspicion.

clue.text: 1960s' comedy disputes stand-up turn

parts.note: pleas are arguments put in a legal dispute

indicators.note: turn means the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: to stand up is to rise

explanation.surface: A stand-up comic's routine argues about a 1960s show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stand-up' looks like comedy but means RISE, which 'turn' reverses. Please Sir! was a British school sitcom from 1968.
explanation.definitionFit: Please Sir! was an ITV sitcom set in a London school, first shown in 1968.

clue.text: Mishchievoush shinger?

definitions.meaning: mischievous said with a lisp: impish, like a pixie
singer with a lisp: the singer Elvis, whose final S a lisper says as SH

explanation.definitionFit: Elvish means impish or mischievous, like an elf; a lisped Elvis gives the same sound.

clue.text: Belief in whatever God made is Man's to apprehend

indicators.note: to apprehend is to catch or seize, so the words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A view that man takes in whatever god he creates.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run through maDE IS Man's.
explanation.definitionFit: Deism is belief in a creator god known through reason rather than revelation.

clue.text: Thoroughly wet Cleese character absorbed by M in new Bond films?

indicators.note: absorbed by means taken inside the following piece

parts.note: Judi Dench played M, the spy chief, in the Bond films from 1995
John Cleese played R, Q's successor, in two Bond films

explanation.surface: John Cleese's role soaks up attention from M in the latest Bond pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: John Cleese played 'R' in The World Is Not Enough; Judi Dench played M from GoldenEye on.
explanation.definitionFit: To drench is to soak something thoroughly.

clue.text: See 16
Gently acting plant disease you and I turned off

indicators.note: off means the next piece is removed

parts.note: mildew is a fungal disease of plants

indicators.note: turned means the word is read backwards

parts.note: you and I together are we

explanation.surface: A gardener turns off a plant disease with a gentle remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes WE into EW, which comes off the end of MILDEW.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild medicine or treatment works gently, without harsh effects.

clue.text: Winter travel time reduced with cunning

parts.note: a sleigh is a vehicle for travel over winter snow
time cut down to its abbreviation is T

explanation.surface: Winter journey time cut through clever planning.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight means cunning or dexterous trickery, as in sleight of hand.

clue.text: Glut of marinated meat on skewers

definitions.meaning: to glut is to fill to excess, satisfy fully
a variant spelling of satay, the South-east Asian dish

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to glut or satisfy, and a variant spelling of satay, skewered grilled meat.

clue.text: Left like Crusoe, producing long yarn

parts.note: Robinson Crusoe was stranded on an isle, an island

explanation.surface: Abandoned like Robinson Crusoe, someone spins a long tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' wants to be a story; it is thread.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, strong cotton thread, a long-stapled yarn.

clue.text: Restless hick to live outside Jerusalem?

indicators.note: outside means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to live is to be, and are is a form of be

indicators.note: restless means unsettled, so these letters are stirred

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A restless country bumpkin heads off to live outside the holy city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restless' scrambles the bumpkin and the little word together, and 'outside' wraps them in a form of 'to be'. 'Jerusalem' is not the city: the Jerusalem artichoke is a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerusalem is the first word of a vegetable's name, so the question mark marks a definition by example.
